title: Temporary Shading Workaround (Vocabulary Type Conflict)
pattern: Renaming (shading) packages to pull two different major versions of the same dependency into a single binary to patch over version conflicts, rather than migrating shared vocabulary types.
why_bad: Type incompatibility. Shading only works for isolated function calls. The moment a type defined in `libbase_v1` is passed to a library expecting `libbase_v2`, the compiler rightly rejects it as a type mismatch. It masks actual design debt and bloats binary footprints.
detection:
The linter must observe:
1. Multiple major versions of the same package imported in a single module or build config.
2. Downstream code forced to write manual mapping wrappers to translate types from version A to version B.
counterexample:
`Context-dependent`
```toml
# Valid: Utilizing the semver trick to re-export common types seamlessly
[dependencies]
libbase = "2.0.0"
```
fix:
Re-architect the package graph to share a unified major version of the vocabulary dependency, utilizing the "semver trick" for transitions when appropriate.
```toml
[dependencies]
libbase = "2.0.0"
```
source:
- Titus Winters et al., *Software Engineering at Google* (2020) [320, 338]
- Jon Gjengset, *Rust for Rustaceans* (2021) [578]
